name: Minigir
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: StressTyp2 archive (StressTyp2-v1-archive-0415 SQL dump), local copy
sources.note: No StressTyp2 entry for Minigir/Vinitiri; the name occurs only in the embedded ISO-code table.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (2012). Change Request 2012-098: [vmg] Minigir -> Lungalunga (submitted by John Grummitt, SIL PNG; adopted 2013-01-23). 6 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; name-change rationale only. Cites as its published source a then-forthcoming SIL Electronic Survey Report: Carter, Carter, Grummitt, Masters, Paris & Paris, 'Gazelle Peninsula Survey of Kairak, Lungalunga, Minigir, Simbali and Taulil' (survey May 2012).

sources.citation: Lynch, John, Malcolm Ross & Terry Crowley (2002). The Oceanic Languages. Richmond: Curzon. (language listing, Meso-Melanesian)
sources.note: Lists 'Minigir (Lungalunga)' with no descriptive source cited (neighbouring Tolai and Patpatar have sources); no sketch, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm (1988). Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of Western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU. (Minigir discussed pp. 257-259 and in ch. 8 sound-correspondence tables)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Nothing on Minigir stress; Minigir appears only in classification (Tolai 'dialect' retaining /s/ and final vowels, treated as a separate language), the village location (Lungalunga, Ataliklikun Bay) and consonant-correspondence tables. The only 'stress' mentions in the book concern Ali (North New Guinea) and general vowel-reduction remarks.

sources.citation: Carter, John, Katie Carter, John Grummitt, Janell Masters, Brian Paris & Hannah Paris (c. 2012-2013). Gazelle Peninsula Survey of Kairak, Lungalunga, Minigir, Simbali and Taulil. SIL Electronic Survey Reports (announced as forthcoming in ISO 639-3 CR 2012-098).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other modern first-hand document on the Lungalunga community; SIL survey reports occasionally include brief phonological notes with the wordlist. Low expected yield for stress but should be checked; publication on SILESR unverified (not in Glottolog 5.1 bib).

sources.citation: Van Der Mark, Sheena Chantal (2007). A grammar of Vinitiri: an Austronesian language of Papua New Guinea. PhD thesis, La Trobe University (RCLT). xx+395 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only reference grammar of the language (Glottolog's sole 'grammar' entry, also Grambank's source); its phonology chapter is where the word-stress statement will be. OPAL record is metadata-only; print copies at La Trobe (Borchardt) and per Glottolog ref 25723 University of Melbourne; Hammarström's collection holds a PDF. Could also be requested from the author or via La Trobe document delivery.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur (1971). The Austronesian languages of Australian New Guinea. In T. Sebeok (ed.), Current Trends in Linguistics 8: 240-340. The Hague: Mouton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Ross 1988:257 credits Capell 1971a with the first notice of the Tolai 'dialect with /s/' (= Minigir); may carry a line on Tolai-area prosody applicable to Minigir, though probably not variety-specific.

sources.citation: Carter, John, Katie Carter, John Grummitt, Janell Masters, Brian Paris & Hannah Paris (c. 2012-2013, 'to be published on SILESR'). Gazelle Peninsula Survey of Kairak, Lungalunga, Minigir, Simbali and Taulil: Recommendations for Participation in the New Britain Initiative. SIL Electronic Survey Reports.
sources.note: Not seen; known only from the ISO change request. sil.org / pnglanguages.sil.1's bib, so publication status is unverified. A sociolinguistic survey; unlikely to carry more than a wordlist.
